verdict.rationale: Plaid's own blog says it is building a 'verify once, verify everywhere' experience (one-click verification) for faster KYC-compliant onboarding, so reuse of a prior verification is a first-party capability. The evidence is only a single marketing-level statement. The /identity_verification/retry endpoint and RETRIED webhook concern re-running a verification, not reusing a passed one, so they earn no credit. missing for 10: developer docs or API reference for recognizing a returning verified user, documented reuse across sessions and products, re-verification policy and expiry rules, consent and data-sharing mechanics, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, a person verified once can be recognized and reused across sessions or products — documented re-verification and reuse of a prior passed check instead of forcing a full re-run

citations.quote: Plaid is creating the standard for a “verify once, verify everywhere” experience that allows companies to offer faster onboarding while remaining KYC compliant.
